search_log: Searched “Gone Before Goodbye” with Maggie, excerpt, Reese Witherspoon, and Harlan Coben; located and opened the publisher’s sustained excerpt and an authorized Barnes & Noble excerpt.

Searched the title with “first person,” “third person,” “point of view,” “narrator,” and “present tense”; found explicit third-person descriptions in a chapter-level structural analysis and a full-book review.

Searched exact interior quote language, including the grief passage, shower passage, and “We’ve made a deal”; results corroborated attribution to the book but did not recover sufficient surrounding context for the clipped first-person-plural passage.
Checked Google Books results, but the available pages supplied catalog descriptions rather than diagnostic narrative prose; the Penguin Random House South Africa extract timed out and was not used.
person_note: The book’s base narration is third person, primarily limited through Maggie and, according to the structural web evidence, shifting to other characters while remaining third person. The publisher-authorized opening independently shows sustained third-person-present narration with access to Maggie’s memories and thoughts, and the interior Goodreads passages likewise narrate specific experiences as “she” and “her.” Generic “you” and “we” aphorisms do not create second- or first-person narrative sections, Porkchop’s “I” is dialogue, and the clipped “We’ve made a deal” passage cannot safely be assigned to the narrator. No credible evidence establishes a sustained first- or second-person base section; the main residual uncertainty is limited context around that clipped passage, which does not outweigh the convergent structural evidence.
